evidence.claim: Western Massachusetts Scenic Byways promotes this state-designated route for its summit views, forest trails and Civilian Conservation Corps architecture.
evidence.quote: At the top you’ll find the rustic stone and wood “parkitecture” of Bascom Lodge, built in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC).

evidence.claim: Automobiles first reached the summit from the north in 1902, when two steam-powered Locomobiles climbed Notch Road.
evidence.quote: The first automobiles to the summit, via the Notch Road from the north, were a pair of steam-powered "Locomobiles' in 1902

evidence.claim: In 1907, the Berkshire County Commission opened a southern road to join that existing approach.
evidence.quote: In 1907, Berkshire County Commission opened a new road from the south to the summit, augmenting the existing northerly "Notch Road."

evidence.claim: The CCC later improved the gravel road system and built much of Bascom Lodge, along with the Thunderbolt Ski Trail and its shelter.
evidence.quote: CCC work included improvements to the road system (gravel surfaced), Adirondack lean-to shelters, the Thunderbolt Ski Shelter and its related trail, along with constructing much of Bascom Lodge.

evidence.claim: Starting in North Adams, the northern approach follows Notch Road toward the summit.

evidence.claim: There, the War Memorial Tower and Bascom Lodge share the summit area with the Thunderbolt Ski Shelter.

evidence.quote: Rockwell Road, which leads to the Visitors' Center, ascends from Lanesborough through Cheshire to the summit in Adams.

evidence.quote: In just under two miles, the trail drops 2,000 feet from Mount Greylock’s summit to its base.

evidence.quote: The Greylock Commission sought a more substantial shelter to replace an earlier summit house (built c.1902; destroyed by fire in 1929).

evidence.quote: The initial west wing was constructed in 1932 by Jules Emil Deloye Jr. The main-central and east wings were completed later 1935–38 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, supervised by Deloye.

flags: Strip miles put the summit at 0.07 beside North Adams despite its mountain position. Used documented northern Notch Road approach, summit stops, then southern Rockwell Road to Lanesborough; summit shelter precedes the tower. Map mileage needs correction.
Sources give summit heights of 3,489 and 3,491 feet and different view distances; omitted numerical height and visibility.

The byway source says championship races continued through the late 1950s; the mountain source documents major races through 1948 and later irregular revivals. Omitted the current championship end date.

Current summit moment attributes the whole lodge to the CCC; revised to distinguish Deloye’s west wing from later CCC work. No current landmark moment was dropped. Seasonal checked date denotes cache review.
